Audit a Rendered PDF Against the Word Version of the Same Report

Source: R/audit_render_parity.R
audit_render_parity.Rd

A lightweight check, run before deliverables are sent out, for the differences that reviewers keep finding between the .pdf and the .docx that Quarto renders from one source. It reads both files and reports, as a table of findings:

margin_overflow

words in the PDF that come closer than margin_in inches to the left or right edge of the page (a formula or a table that runs out of the text area).

numbering

table or figure numbers that are missing from one of the two files or that are not consecutive in one of them.

order

table and figure captions that come in another order in the PDF than in the Word file.

caption_placement

a table caption that is above the table in one file and below it in the other.

numbers

percentages and decimal numbers that occur in one file and not in the other (for example 98.9% in the PDF and 97% in Word), counted, so a number that occurs twice in one file and once in the other is reported.

A check that could not be made (a table that could not be found, or found in more than one place, in the PDF) is listed as info.

Usage

audit_render_parity(
  pdf_path,
  docx_path,
  margin_in = 0.5,
  check = c("margins", "numbering", "order", "placement", "numbers"),
  docx_limits = NULL
)

Arguments

pdf_path

Path to the rendered .pdf.

docx_path

Path to the rendered .docx.

margin_in

Minimum distance, in inches, between text and the left and right edge of a PDF page (default 0.5).

check

Which checks to run: any of "margins", "numbering", "order", "placement", "numbers". Default all.

docx_limits

NULL or a named list of limits on the Word archive; see docx_review_extract().

Value

A tibble of class render_parity with the columns check, severity ("warning" or "info"), location (for example "page 3" or "Table 2") and detail. No rows means nothing was found. Attributes: n_pages, captions (the captions found in each file).

Details

This reads text and positions only; it does not look at the pages. It is meant to point at places to look at, not to certify a document. It was checked against reports rendered by Quarto (PDF through LaTeX, Word through pandoc); Word files written by hand in Word, other PDF engines and two-column layouts are less tested.

  • A caption is a line (PDF) or paragraph (Word) that begins with Table, Figure or Fig. (any case), a number, and a ., :, en dash or em dash followed by a space. A sentence that begins "Table 1 shows" or "Table 1.5 mg were given" is not a caption. Quarto's non-breaking space after the word is read as a space. Supplementary numbers (Table S1) and panels (Figure 1A) are not recognised. A caption repeated on the continuation pages of a long table counts once.

  • Quarto wraps each cross-referenced table and figure in a one-cell layout table; the wrapper is looked through. A table is a table of the Word file when it has at least two cells and no table inside it. Content controls are read.

  • The place of a table in the PDF is found from the first row of its header, within a page of its caption, and not from a line that another caption is nearer to. A header that occurs in two places near the caption, or a table whose first cell is empty, gives an info row.

  • Not read: text boxes, headers and footers of the Word file. Footnotes and endnotes of the Word file are read, because the PDF holds them in its text. Lines of the PDF that repeat on at least half of its pages (running headers and footers), the lines of its contents lists (a line that ends in dot leaders and a page number) and section numbers at the start of a line are left out of the comparison of numbers; so are the contents paragraphs of the Word file.

  • Pages that the PDF stores rotated (landscape pages made by pdflscape and similar) are measured in their displayed width. Two-column layouts are not understood: lines are read across the columns, so captions in the second column can be missed.

  • PDF text is as extracted by pdftools: a number that the PDF engine splits across lines can appear as a difference. Positions are whole points, so margin_in has a tolerance of 2 points.

The Word file is an untrusted archive and is read with the same size limits as docx_review_extract() (docx_limits); no entity is expanded and no network is used.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- audit_render_parity("report.pdf", "report.docx")
res
} # }
